_notes.what this is: The PPO run on the 64-vCPU box (g6e.16xlarge, one L40S 46 GB, on demand, $7.58 an hour, launched 2026-10-05 11:32 UTC in another person's AWS account). Read by pipeline.py (everything but "eval") and by evaluate.py ("eval"). The live copy is ~/runs/main/run.json on the box, outside the code, so a new release cannot reset it.
_notes.history: Imitation of PSBot ran by hand to 27.5M decisions (checkpoint learner_update_000745.pt, kept in phase_final/). Warmup ran by hand for 2.2M decisions (learner_update_000060.pt, kept in phase_final/). Both phases are marked skip so the supervisor starts in PPO and resumes the newest PPO checkpoint.
_notes.servers.count, train_defaults.battles: 44 servers. Measured on this box with release r1: warmup at 44 x 32 battles gave 3,500 decisions a second with 14 of 64 threads busy; the single inference thread is the limit, so more battles per server (a bigger batch per inference call) is the lever. 44 x 64 = 2816.
_notes.phases.ppo.target_decisions: 600,000,000: about 42 hours at 4,000 a second. The plan stops the box at 72 hours, at this count, or on a plateau, whichever comes first.
_notes.train_defaults.save_every: Every 25 updates is about every 4 minutes at this speed.
_notes.watchdog.recycle_hours: A planned clean restart every 6 hours.
_notes.retention: On: newest 8, everything younger than 8 hours, every 250th update, each phase's last, and everything an evaluation names.
_notes.on_done: shutdown: when PPO reaches its target, wait for the final evaluation, then halt the box (it stops, the disk stays).
_notes.on_failed: idle for now: a failed run leaves the box up for a person to look at. The 2-hourly check-in reads status.py.
_notes.eval: Every 3 hours: 400 games against each of simple and psbot, 100 against random and maxpower would add nothing, so they are left out. Foul Play: 200 games every 3 hours on 8 cores (training leaves about 45 threads idle).
